Cross-system handoffs shall include a correlation/reference ID so source and target events can be reconciled. 36. Cross-Role Handoffs & Inter-Module Workflows 36.1 QC → Vendor Manager Quality Escalation Requirement ID
Step 1 QC identifies repeated or critical vendor/SKU defect and records standardized defects plus evidence.
Step 2 QC creates Vendor Manager escalation referencing impacted QC cases, SKU, vendor and recommended corrective action.
Step 3 Vendor Manager reviews vendor performance context and creates vendor corrective-action/follow-up plan.
Step 4 Vendor response and corrective actions are linked back to the escalation.
Step 5 QC performs recheck or monitors subsequent quality trend before escalation closure where applicable.
Step 1 Customer disputes a return/QC outcome through a Help Desk ticket.
Step 2 Help Desk verifies requester and links order, return and QC case; customer statement is preserved verbatim.
Step 3 Help Desk creates QC escalation with dispute reason and any customer evidence.
Step 4 QC Manager reviews original inspection, evidence and policy; any recheck/override is separately audited.
Step 5 Help Desk receives the reviewed outcome and communicates the approved customer-facing resolution. 36.3 Help Desk → Vendor Manager Vendor Issue
Step 1 Help Desk detects seller-related delay, repeated cancellation, conduct issue or unresolved vendor dependency.
Step 2 Help Desk creates linked Vendor Manager escalation containing ticket/order/vendor references and evidence.
Step 3 Vendor Manager coordinates vendor response and records action plan or resolution.
Step 4 Help Desk receives resolution status and communicates the customer-facing outcome without exposing internal notes.
Step 1 Vendor raises a payment, settlement, fee, commercial or protected status issue with Vendor Manager.
Step 2 Vendor Manager captures structured request, evidence and business justification.
Step 3 The system routes the request to the authoritative Accounts/Super Admin workflow rather than applying a direct change.
Step 4 Decision and implementation reference return to Vendor Manager for vendor communication and closure. 36.5 Help Desk → Accounts Refund Investigation
Step 1 Help Desk verifies order/payment/refund IDs and confirms that the expected credit window has passed or a failure state exists.
Step 2 Help Desk creates a finance investigation with safe customer statement and references.
Step 3 Accounts reconciles provider/bank status in the Accounts portal.
Step 4 Help Desk receives a support-safe result and updates the customer ticket. 37. Integrations & External Service Behaviour
The portal shall consume order, payment, refund, shipment, vendor, catalog, stock and QC source data through authenticated APIs/events rather than local unsynchronised copies where practicable.
Webhook/event consumers shall be idempotent and shall not duplicate tickets, QC cases or tasks on repeated delivery.
External communication provider failures shall be visible with retry status and shall not falsely mark a message delivered.
Telephony/chat integrations shall preserve provider IDs and timestamps for troubleshooting.
Carrier tracking shall show provider/source timestamp and latest synchronisation time.
Cross-system status updates shall handle delayed/out-of-order events using version or event-time rules.
Integration errors affecting a user action shall return a recoverable error and correlation ID; irreversible partial actions shall be prevented or reconciled.
API access shall be permission-scoped and sensitive fields filtered server-side, not only hidden in the UI. 38. Privacy, Security & Data Handling Requirement ID
Customer and vendor personal data shall be displayed on a need-to-know basis and masked by default.
Users shall not be allowed to capture payment secrets such as CVV, OTP, PIN or account passwords in structured fields or notes.
Sensitive free-text fields shall display warnings and may apply automated redaction rules where configured.
Download links for sensitive attachments shall be authenticated, time-limited where appropriate and logged.
Record access shall be enforced server-side using role and data scope.
Attachment upload shall validate MIME type, file signature, size and malware scan status.
Personally identifiable information in exports shall be minimized and protected by access policy.
Data retention/deletion requests shall route to the authoritative privacy workflow; operational users shall not manually purge source records outside policy.
Users shall be able to report suspected security/privacy incidents through an internal escalation path.
Application logs shall avoid recording secrets and unnecessary full PII. 39. Validation, Error Handling & Concurrency Requirement ID
All mandatory fields shall be validated on client and server; server validation is authoritative.
Validation errors shall identify the affected field and provide a corrective message without exposing implementation details.
If a record has changed since the user opened it, destructive/state-changing updates shall detect the conflict and require refresh/review.
Double-click/retry of state-changing actions shall be idempotent or protected from duplicate processing.
Long-running exports/imports shall execute as background jobs with status and downloadable result/error file.
Partial bulk failures shall not roll back successful independent items unless transaction semantics require all-or-nothing behavior.
If an integration is unavailable, the UI shall distinguish temporary technical failure from business rejection.
Failed communications shall remain retryable and shall not be displayed as delivered.
Offline/stale source data shall display last synchronised time when material to user decisions.
Irreversible actions shall require a confirmation dialog describing impact and required reason where applicable. 40. Non-Functional Requirements Requirement ID
Primary list and detail screens should meet agreed performance targets under expected concurrent load; backend pagination is required for large datasets.
Critical operational actions shall provide visible completion/failure feedback without requiring manual page refresh.
The web application shall support current enterprise desktop browsers and responsive layouts for standard laptop resolutions.
Keyboard navigation, focus states, labels, error associations and contrast shall meet the project accessibility standard.
Service availability, backup, disaster recovery, RPO and RTO shall follow Shopeye production infrastructure standards.
Operational logs and metrics shall support monitoring of API latency, error rates, background jobs, integrations and SLA calculation health.
User-facing dates/times shall use configured timezone and clear date-time formats while storing canonical timestamps server-side.
Amounts and percentages displayed from source systems shall use consistent currency/rounding rules and shall not be independently recalculated by Help Desk or Vendor Manager UI unless specified.
All requirement-controlled actions shall be testable through deterministic acceptance criteria and auditable server responses.
Feature flags may be used for staged rollout but must not bypass authorization. 41. Recommended Status Models Entity
Status transitions shall be explicitly validated; users shall not be able to jump to invalid states through UI or API.
Each transition shall record actor, timestamp, source, reason where required and previous/new state.
Automatic transitions shall identify the system/rule as actor and preserve the triggering event.
Reopening a closed entity shall not erase its prior closure/resolution history. 42. Recommended Web Screen Inventory Area
UI/UX screens cover all mandatory fields, states, empty/loading/error conditions and permission variants.
Backend APIs enforce the same permissions and validation rules as the UI.
All state-changing actions produce the required audit trail and correlation IDs.
Cross-role handoffs are tested end-to-end with source/target status consistency.
Integration failure and retry scenarios are tested without duplicate side effects.
PII masking, export restrictions and sensitive attachment access are security-tested.
UAT scenarios are executed with documented results and critical/high defects resolved or formally accepted.
Operational reports reconcile to source records for sampled periods.

Order status shall distinguish commercial order state from shipment/logistics state where needed.

Required-field errors shall appear adjacent to the field and prevent invalid submission.
Email, phone, tax IDs, bank routing codes, postal codes and URLs shall use configurable jurisdiction-appropriate validation.
Numeric inputs shall enforce min/max/precision and reject malformed numbers.
Date ranges shall enforce logical ordering and relevant business cutoffs.
File uploads shall validate type, extension, MIME, size and malware/security policy.
Rich-text inputs shall be sanitized to block scripts/unsafe markup.
Duplicate identifiers such as SKU, location code or role name shall return clear non-sensitive errors.
Cross-field validation shall run both client-side for usability and server-side for security/correctness. Shopeye • Confidential • Vendor & Vendor Staff Web SRS v1.0 • 36
API/network failures shall preserve safe user inputs and provide retry guidance without duplicate processing.
Critical write operations shall use idempotency or equivalent protection against double submission.
Concurrent edits to sensitive records should detect stale versions and require refresh/merge rather than silently overwrite.
Bulk jobs shall provide row-level errors and partial-success summary where partial processing is supported.
Provider outages shall distinguish platform error from validation error and preserve retryable work.
Unauthorized actions shall return a generic access error without revealing protected record existence.
All errors shall have a support-friendly correlation/reference ID where operationally useful. 38. Security, Privacy & Data Protection 38.1 Security Controls Req ID
Enforce TLS for all authenticated portal traffic and secure cookie/token settings.
Hash passwords using an industry-standard adaptive password hashing algorithm; never store plaintext passwords.
Encrypt sensitive vendor/customer financial and identity data at rest where required.
Apply role-based access control and vendor-tenant isolation to every server-side data query/action.
Use CSRF protection, output encoding, content security controls and input validation appropriate to the web architecture.
Rate-limit authentication, OTP, password reset, exports, search and sensitive endpoints as appropriate.
Require step-up authentication for high-risk actions such as bank change, owner security change, ownership transfer or API secret rotation.
Scan uploaded documents/media for malicious content and store them with non-guessable secured references.
Mask bank, tax and customer PII unless full value is required and user has explicit permission.
Record security-relevant events and support incident investigation with correlation IDs. 38.2 Privacy & Retention Controls Req ID
Customer data visible to vendor shall be limited to the minimum needed for fulfilment, support and legal obligations.
Customer contact information should use masking/relay where marketplace model supports it.
Export permissions for customer/order data shall be restricted and auditable.
Vendor/staff personal data retention and deletion shall follow platform privacy/legal obligations while preserving required audit/financial records.
Financial/tax documents and audit logs may be retained independently of account deactivation according to statutory policy.

Privacy requests affecting vendor staff data shall be routed through controlled platform process when self-service cannot lawfully complete deletion. 39. Non-Functional Requirements 39.1 Performance & Scalability
Primary authenticated pages should meet defined performance targets under normal expected load.
Large lists shall use server-side pagination/filtering and indexed search strategies.
Large exports/imports/reports shall execute asynchronously and not block interactive requests.
Order, stock and financial write paths shall maintain consistency under concurrent vendor activity.
The architecture shall scale by vendor, catalog, order and staff volume without cross-tenant degradation beyond agreed limits. 39.2 Availability & Reliability Req ID
Critical order/fulfilment functions shall have defined availability and recovery objectives.
External-provider failures shall use retries/circuit-breaking/idempotency as appropriate without duplicating business transactions.
Background jobs shall expose failure state and controlled retry/recovery.
Backup and recovery processes shall cover vendor operational and financial data according to platform RPO/RTO.
Monitoring shall detect elevated error rates, job backlogs, provider outages and fulfilment event failures. 39.3 Accessibility & UX Req ID
Portal shall support current major desktop browsers and responsive use on common tablet widths unless product scope says otherwise.
Keyboard navigation, focus order, labels, contrast and semantic controls shall follow the platform accessibility target.
Validation errors shall be understandable and associated with relevant controls.
Destructive or irreversible actions shall require clear confirmation and consequence messaging.
Financial values, dates, timezones and statuses shall use consistent formatting throughout the portal. 40. Vendor Owner vs Vendor Staff Capability Matrix Req ID
